info.description:
## Authorization
We use bearer auth throughout the API. Generally, API requests should have the follow header:  
{  
    "content-type": "application/json",  
    "Authorization": "Bearer TOKEN_GOES_HERE"  
}  
Please refer to the Auth section immediately below for details on getting your token.

get.description:

You will need to have the following data accesses assigned to your user to use this route: mm_get_auditlogs

parameters.description:

You can use brackets and a comma to perform an ‘OR’ search e.g [a,b*] will search for ‘a’ OR a value starting with ‘b’. You can also use the '$isNull' value to retrieve the records that does not have an externalKey set by the current user.

search.name: search
search.description:
This does an advanced search using a url encoded JSON object.

Most fields available in the return object can be searched using this methodology.
Example: search={ "status": "active"} would search the status field for the value: 'active'.

Searching is also possible using nested fields. Use the following syntax: <object>.<field> to specify the nested field.
Example: search={ "Stock.name": "Best Beer" }

There are a couple of extra operators that can be used in the search. These are $or, $and, $not.
Example: search={ "$or": [ { "status": "bad" }, { "status": "worse" } ] }. Searches for the statuses of 'bad' or 'worse'.
The $or, $and and $not operators can be nested.

If the name pair contains a fieldName it is possible for the value to be a sub-object containing any number of operators. The operators depend on the fieldType of the fieldName:

Date time Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in
Example: search={ "startTime": { "$gt": "2 November 2021" } }

Relative Date time Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in
Example: search={ "startTime": { "$gt": "2 November 2021" } }
This 'relativeDateTime' field is relative to the timezone a user resides in and is not an absolute point in time

Number Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $not, $or, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $between, $notBetween, $in, $notIn
Example: search={ "totalCount": { "$gt": 10 } }

String Allowed Operators: $eq, $ne, $is, $not, $or, $in, $like, $iLike, $notLike, $notILike, $notIn
Example: search={ "failReason": { "$in": ["Out of bounds", "Out of time"] } }

These operators equate to Sequelize operators. See Operators | Sequelize
